hook.line: Vale can make a perfect pastry blindfolded, while Tomás can barely follow a recipe in Spanish. Spanish doesn't say someone *is* good at something. It says the thing *gives itself well* to them.
hook.es: A Vale se le dan muy bien los pasteles.
hook.en: Vale is really good at pastries.

examples.es: A Vale se le dan muy bien los pasteles.
examples.en: Vale is really good at pastries.

examples.es: A mí se me dan mal los números.

examples.en: Are you good at driving? (to a friend)

examples.es: Mariana tiene facilidad para los idiomas.

examples.es: A Tomás se le da mal esperar.

rule:
English says "I'm good at it". Spanish says "it gives itself well to me": *Se me da bien cocinar*.

The person is *me, te, le, nos, les*. Add *a Vale* or *a mí* to name or stress who.

The skill is what *se da*, so a plural skill makes the verb plural: *Se me dan mal los números*. A verb stays singular: *Se me da bien cocinar*.

Another way: *tener facilidad para* + noun: *Mariana tiene facilidad para los idiomas*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a *gustar*-type construction: the skill is the subject and the person is the indirect object.

yourTurn.prompt: Talking about yourself, choose *me* or *te*: Se ___ da bien cocinar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: *Me* is the person it gives itself to: you.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *da* or *dan*: A mí se me ___ mal los números. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: A mí se me dan mal los números.
yourTurn.why: *Números* is plural, so the verb is *dan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *da* or *dan*: Se me ___ bien cocinar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: A verb counts as one thing, so *da*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Are you good at driving?
accept: ¿A ti se te da bien manejar?
yourTurn.why: *Te* is the friend, and *manejar* stays plain.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale is really good at pastries.
yourTurn.answer: A Vale se le dan muy bien los pasteles.
yourTurn.why: *A Vale* names the person, *le* repeats it, and *pasteles* is plural, so *dan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about Tomás: *Se me da mal esperar.*
yourTurn.answer: A Tomás se le da mal esperar.
accept: Se le da mal esperar a Tomás.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about us: *Se me da bien el español.*
yourTurn.answer: Se nos da bien el español.
accept: A nosotros se nos da bien el español.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The skill is the thing doing the giving, and you are *me*.

pitfalls.wrong: Se me da mal los números.
pitfalls.right: Se me dan mal los números.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Números* is plural, so the verb is *dan*.

pitfalls.wrong: A Vale se la da bien cocinar.
pitfalls.right: A Vale se le da bien cocinar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The person is always *le* (to her), never *la*.

personal: Say one thing that comes easily to you and one that doesn't: *Se me da bien…* and *Se me da mal…*
